headline: High: shared project-directory writes and OpenBB MCP/API ingestion create default-path data leakage and cascading-error risk; prompt injection is lower but present via file-based handoff.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: gpt-engineer writes files in a shared project directory and OpenBBTerminal can consume inputs via MCP/REST APIs, so file-based handoff can carry attacker-controlled instructions into B. The pair lacks provenance tracking or isolation by default, making injection plausible beyond manual copy-paste.
conditions: IF agent_a writes prompt-like text into the shared project directory and agent_b reads it as instructions
IF agent_b ingests MCP/API payloads without provenance checks
mitigations: Separate the project directory from any B ingestion path
Add a manual review step before B consumes A-generated files
Disable MCP ingestion for untrusted file content
Prefix A outputs with machine-readable delimiters and ignore free text
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between file writes and downstream parsing

B_data_leakage.rationale: agent_a reads and writes the project directory and can handle OPENAI_API_KEY, while agent_b touches financial, licensed, and public data and exposes MCP/REST APIs. A shared workspace or copied artifacts could move sensitive code or data between them, and B's API surfaces increase exposure. The profiles do not show isolation.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same project directory or copied workspace
IF sensitive financial or licensed data is placed into files that agent_a can read
mitigations: Use separate directories for A and B
Keep secrets out of shared files and env dumps
Restrict B inputs to synthetic or redacted data
Review any file before passing it from A to B
requires-engineering: enforce workspace-level access controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: gpt-engineer has broad filesystem write and shell execution, while OpenBBTerminal has no filesystem write, no shell, and no subprocess spawning. Their write surfaces do not overlap, so direct concurrent mutation conflict is limited. The only shared mutable surface shown is the project directory via agent_a, which B does not write.
conditions: IF agent_b is extended with write access to the same directory
IF an external orchestrator grants both agents mutable access to one shared state store
mitigations: Keep B read-only relative to A's project directory
Avoid concurrent edits to the same files
Serialize any handoff between agents
Use separate working trees
requires-engineering: add locking if B gains write access

D_cascading_error.rationale: gpt-engineer produces generated code and OpenBBTerminal can consume data through MCP/REST APIs, so A's output can become B's input without a built-in verification step. If B treats A-generated artifacts as authoritative, mistakes or fabricated code/data can cascade into downstream actions or analyses. The profiles do not show a critical evaluator between them.
conditions: IF agent_b consumes agent_a output without independent validation
IF A-generated code or facts are used to drive B's analysis or actions
mitigations: Require a human review before B uses A output
Validate schemas and types on all handoffs
Compare A output against source data before acting
Log and diff A-to-B transfers
requires-engineering: add automated verification gates

E_compliance.rationale: agent_b explicitly touches financial and licensed data, while agent_a can read/write project files and execute generated code with the user's privileges. If regulated or licensed data is placed into A's workspace, the pair can create a compliance breach through uncontrolled local handling and model/API exposure. No residency or retention controls are documented for either agent.
conditions: IF financial or licensed data is copied into agent_a's project directory
IF either agent retains or logs regulated data outside the intended policy boundary
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of A's workspace
Use redacted or synthetic datasets
Review retention settings before any run
Confirm data-processing agreements for B
requires-engineering: add residency and retention enforcement
